---
title: "The Essence of Data Visualisation"
subtitle: "PyCon Africa 2026"
---

A plot uses position, size or colour to show data. A table uses text,
layout and formatting. In both, we choose how a value appears on the page.
We call this a *mapping*.

In this workshop, you'll build plots with plotnine and tables with
great-tables. You'll use data from the Uganda census to explore how these
choices can help readers notice an error.

By the end, you should be able to:

- Explain which data values control what you see in a plot or table.
- Build plots with plotnine and tables with great-tables.
- Choose a plot or table to suit your readers.
- Use a visualisation to spot figures that need checking.

## Getting ready

The workshop runs in your browser. You don't need to install anything.
Python can take a minute to load when you first open a page. Open the
workshop pages now so they're ready when we reach them.

You can edit and run the exercise code on each page. If you'd prefer to
work on your own machine, install the packages with:

```bash
uv add plotnine great-tables pandas
```
